chain.label: COA failed to correct known SOP/checklist noncompliance
chain.trigger: the inadequate remedial actions by COA to ensure adherence to standard operating procedures

chain.label: FAA oversight of COA inadequate to detect procedural deviations
chain.trigger: the Federal Aviation Administration's inadequate oversight of COA to ensure adherence to standard operating procedures

chain.label: Hydraulics item buried in checklist; low-pressure mode silently disables gear and flaps
chain.trigger: the 'Hydraulics' item is placed too low on the in-range checklist, rendering it vulnerable to omission... without providing an overt signal to the flightcrew of the non-functional status of those components

chain.label: Both pilots short of sleep after early wakeup on layover
chain.trigger: The captain had the opportunity for 6 to 6.5 hours of sleep, and... the first officer had the opportunity for only 5.5 hours of sleep

chain.label: Manuals and training never stated that pumps left in LOW disable gear and flaps
chain.trigger: the flight manual and training materials do not explicitly state that if the pumps are not switched to 'HI,' the landing gear will not extend and the flaps will not deploy

caused_by.evidence: COA was aware of inconsistencies in flightcrew adherence to standard operating procedures... corrective actions taken before the accident had not resolved this problem

chain.label: In-range checklist not properly completed; Hydraulics item omitted and not cross-checked
chain.trigger: the captain referred to each of the seven items on the in-range checklist... except for the fourth item, 'Hydraulics,' to which the captain did not refer

caused_by.evidence: an operational climate may have existed in which crews occasionally deviated from standard operating procedures
the 'Hydraulics' item is placed too low on the in-range checklist, rendering it vulnerable to omission
the flightcrew's degraded performance is consistent with the effects of fatigue

chain.label: Hydraulic systems left in low-pressure mode; gear and flaps unpowered
chain.trigger: Because the hydraulic system remained in the low pressure mode, hydraulic pressure was not available to lower the landing gear and deploy the flaps

caused_by.evidence: because the captain omitted the 'Hydraulics' item on the in-range checklist and the first officer failed to detect the error, hydraulic pressure was not available

chain.label: Flaps failed to extend at any setting; airplane never decelerated, approach unstabilized
chain.trigger: Only the leading edge slats deployed because of the low hydraulic pressure... 34 seconds before touchdown, the airplane was 504 feet AFE and traveling at 216 knots indicated airspeed

caused_by.evidence: hydraulic pressure was not available to lower the landing gear and deploy the flaps

chain.label: Crew missed hydraulic caution cues and never diagnosed the configuration error
chain.trigger: the flightcrew failed to detect that the flaps had not extended to 5o... the captain's distraction from his duties as pilot-in-command and his disregard for the sterile cockpit rule contributed to the pilots' failure to detect their hydraulic system configuration error

caused_by.evidence: The failure of the flaps to extend to 5o was an important cue that the hydraulic system was not properly configured

the pilots' lack of previous exposure, either through training or during line operations, to the consequences of improper hydraulic system configuration contributed to their failure to detect their hydraulic system configuration error
his inability to effectively process the rapidly changing information concerning abnormal system operation are consistent with the effects of fatigue
The captain's disregard for the sterile cockpit rule also raises concerns that an operational climate tolerant of nonstandard conduct may have existed at COA

chain.label: Landing checklist never performed; gear position unconfirmed and warning horn ignored
chain.trigger: The landing checklist was not performed, and the flightcrew did not confirm that the gear was down and locked. The gear warning horn sounded during the approach... but it was ignored

caused_by.evidence: The increase in speed allowed the flightcrew very little time to address the flap problem and configure the airplane for landing
the pilots failed to perform the landing checklist and to detect the numerous cues alerting them to the status of the landing gear as a result of their focus on coping with the flap extension problem
Fatigue can interfere with an individual's capability to deal with rapidly changing events and to direct and sustain attention

chain.label: Captain refused the go-around and continued the unstabilized approach through GPWS alerts
chain.trigger: the captain's decision to continue the approach contrary to COA standard operating procedures that mandate a go-around when an approach is unstabilized below 500 feet or a ground proximity warning system alert continues below 200 feet above field elevation

caused_by.evidence: The approach was clearly unstabilized when the airplane descended through 500 feet; yet, the flightcrew failed to discontinue the approach
Unaware that the gear was not down, the captain assumed control of the airplane and made a wheels-up landing
The captain's deficient decisionmaking at the end of the flight... are consistent with the effects of fatigue
He repeatedly deviated from standard operating procedures, failed to adhere to the sterile cockpit rule, ignored warnings, and did not utilize effective CRM techniques

chain.label: First officer did not challenge the captain's decision to continue
chain.trigger: the first officer did not challenge the captain's statement. He also did not question the captain to determine his reason(s) for continuing the approach

caused_by.evidence: When the captain denied the first officer's request to go around and told him to keep his speed up, the first officer did not challenge the captain's statement

chain.label: Wheels-up touchdown at 193 knots, substantial fuselage damage
chain.trigger: the airplane touched down hard with the wheels up at 193 knots indicated airspeed... The airplane received substantial damage to its lower fuselage

caused_by.evidence: there was no compelling reason for the captain's decision to land the airplane; multiple signals and guidance indicated that the approach should be discontinued
had the landing checklist been properly performed, the flightcrew would have detected the failure of the landing gear to extend
although the first officer was unwilling to overtly challenge the captain's decision to continue the approach, he did attempt to communicate his concern

chain.label: Airplane slid 6,850 feet and departed the runway into the grass
chain.trigger: The airplane slid 6,850 feet before coming to rest in the grass about 140 feet left of the runway centerline

caused_by.evidence: A continuous scrape mark started at this point and led down the runway... departing from the pavement about 6,730 feet after it began

chain.label: Cabin filled with smoke; 12 passengers minor injuries during evacuation
chain.trigger: The cabin began to fill with smoke, and the captain ordered the evacuation of the airplane... 12 minor injuries to passengers were reported

caused_by.evidence: two controllers on duty in the tower and two airport groundskeepers observed smoke and fire coming from beneath the airplane
The airplane came to a stop in the grass off to the left side of the runway
